original_independent_report:
# Independent fixed cost measurements

Frozen target 73d1b00067822f09f654e9541dea495ddb89a2a4. Three sequential QEMU cold boots per cell, 24 accepted, zero guest failures. All 24 earlier capture-wrapper invocations stopped before launching QEMU due to a precreated directory. Their original logs are under prelaunch. Each accepted boot met the UART gate and its stopped PC lay inside the linked idle function.

The four configured stacks include the 832-byte fabricated frame. Slot 3 remained all zero in each of the twelve cost-enabled captures. Each image reserves 81920 bytes for five stacks. Cost-enabled images also reserve 7208 journal bytes. The boot stack occupies a separate 16384 bytes. Changed-byte depth can underestimate stack use through coincidental paint, restoration and unused stack-pointer adjustments.

The counter includes parts of the Rust handler and the complete inner policy event. Vector entry, saves, restores, ERET and handler prologue/epilogue are outside the sampled interval. Trace publication, decoding, timer servicing and sampling instructions can affect the inclusive outer measurements. Appending a journal entry after the endpoint can affect later scheduling. Calibration is one ordered counter pair per boot, with no subtraction. Convert ticks using ticks × 1e9 / frequency. Cost-off images establish behavior and static footprint only. The samples do not establish runtime overhead relative to the uninstrumented kernel, cross-cell speed rankings, worst-case bounds, board performance or qualification.

Run python3 verify.py to reconstruct observations.json. Each event row gives group, incoming/selected frame addresses, four ordered counter endpoints, outer/inner ticks and cumulative group maxima within that run. Slot depth arrays retain boot order. Per-ELF PT_LOAD ranges, section sizes, all symbols, ELF binaries and corresponding build logs are included. The candidate patch and tracked working-tree patch are supplied. working-tree-status.txt records the untracked Python cache.

archive.format: Ordered byte chunks of one DEFLATE ZIP; each linked JSON stores base64 and SHA-256
archive.restore_python:
import pathlib,json,base64,hashlib,io,zipfile
p=pathlib.Path('evd-041.json'); m=json.loads(p.read_bytes())['archive']; parts=[]
for name in m['parts']:
    row=json.loads((p.parent/name).read_bytes()); data=base64.b64decode(row['data'],validate=True); assert hashlib.sha256(data).hexdigest()==row['sha256']; parts.append(data)
b=b''.join(parts); assert hashlib.sha256(b).hexdigest()==m['sha256']
with zipfile.ZipFile(io.BytesIO(b)) as z:
    assert all(hashlib.sha256(z.read(n)).hexdigest()==h for n,h in m['entry_sha256'].items()); z.extractall('evd-041-raw')
archive.offline_replay: Execute restore_python with Python 3 from the JSON directory, then python evd-041-raw/verify_tables.py. It reads the retained nm, section and segment tables and all captures, recalculating observations.json without ELF binaries. Original verify.py requires each matching ELF at its cell/kernel.elf path, verifies its recorded SHA-256 and performs the same decoding. Archived build_cost_matrix.py, run.py, index.json and versions.txt record original build and capture settings.
